summary: The week saw continued momentum around the 1952 "Invasion of Washington" UFO tape as lawmakers pushed for its release, with some suggesting it could surface soon. Meanwhile, Luis Elizondo stepped back into the spotlight with fresh allegations, recalling a congressional staffer's warning about a plan to "eliminate" him while navigating questions about his own role in government secrecy efforts. On the military side, defense officials acknowledged that UAP sightings over U.S. bases have left the military genuinely stumped, with some incidents suggesting the objects may want to be observed. A separate missing persons case drew attention when a retired lab worker connected to quantum physics disappeared, and a missing general reportedly tried to resign before his disappearance due to unexplained "brain fog." AARO released new documents this week including privacy assessments and case files examining starlink correlations and observation methodology, while experts renewed calls for legal protections to shield whistleblowers from retaliation.
